title: kv-cache-seqlen-edgecase-breadcrumbs
content:
Scratchpad / breadcrumbs for sequence-length edge-case that causes KV cache corruption + attention kernel mismatch

Problem summary:
- Intermittent token duplication and truncated outputs when resuming from KV cache on long sequences (>8192 tokens) with specific prompt shapes.
- Seems to correlate with kernel selection path: fallback from Triton flash-attn -> cuBLAS matmul path when seq_len crosses threshold.

Observed behavior:
- Repro (local): run ./tools/repro --model llama2-13b --max-seq 9000 --batch 1 --resume-kv true
  -> after ~512 tokens into continuation, repeated subsequence (same 6 tokens) appears, then generation stalls.
- Logs show: WARNING kernel_selector: fallback to generic_attention (why?), kernel config: {block_size: 64, split_qkv: true}
- GPU memory reports OK; KV cache sizes look correct except for 'write_ptr' observed lower than expected in dump_kv( )

Commands tried:
1) baseline repro (docker): docker run --gpus all -e MODEL=llama2-13b repro:latest ./run --seqlen 9000
2) kernel forcing: export RW_KERNEL_FORCE=flash_attn ; run -> success (no corruption)
3) force other kernel: RW_KERNEL_FORCE=generic_attention -> corruption reproduces reliably
4) lowered batch size and disable batching -> still reproduces
5) quantized model path -> corruption less frequent but present
6) flush-kv between prompts (workaround) -> mitigates but not ideal

Error snippets:
- "KVCache: write_ptr (0x7ffcd) > storage_end (0x7ffab)" in debug dump
- "kernel_selector: kernel mismatch: expected flash_attn, got generic_attention for seq_len=8672"

Hypotheses / notes:
- Kernel selection heuristic probably uses estimated peak_seq_len based on request metadata; with certain rolling-sum inputs it misestimates and selects wrong kernel.
- generic_attention path has slightly different indexing for KV write loops -> off-by-N when seq_len not multiple of tile-size -> memory overwrite at page boundary.
- When flash_attn chosen, code uses fused qkv layout that avoids separate KV write; when fallback, separate KV write routine used and has a bug for large offsets.

Next experiments to run (prio order):
- Add assert checks in generic_attention write loop: bounds check on write_ptr vs storage_end (quick safety net)
- Re-run repro with tracing: RW_KV_DUMP=1 RW_KV_TRACE=1 -> capture exact index writes
- Force kernel_selector to choose kernels by exact_seq_len not heuristics (patch locally) and repro
- Create minimal C++ loop reproducer (unit test) to isolate indexing arithmetic (no CUDA)
- Try different page-alignment of KV storage (align to 2MB) to see if overwrite disappears

Quick diffs to try (local branches):
- runtime/attention/generic_attention.cpp: add size_t remaining = storage_end - write_ptr; if (write_count > remaining) log error + clamp
- runtime/kernel_selector.cpp: log decision inputs (estimated_seq_len, token_histogram) to reproduce bad heuristic

Notes for postmortem:
- Affects Dedicated + Private deployments where long-document summarization is common
- Workaround: bump kernel selection threshold to prefer flash_attn for seq_len>4096 until fix
- Customer impact: truncation/duplication reported in tickets REDW-3142, REDW-3190

Links/reference:
- github PR with previous similar fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1122
- Slack thread: #eng-serving-runtime thread 'kv corrupt analysis' (link in linked_artifacts)

Open questions:
- Why is quantized path less frequent? different memory layout or smaller KV element size?
- Could prefetching or caching policy change timing that masks the bug?
- Need reviewer: @Diego for kernel indexing, @Maya for KV layout

Immediate todo (today):
- add bounds-assert patch + run unit repro (Samira)
- collect full kv trace from failing customer run and upload to S3
- coordinate with support for mitigation docs

-- end scratchpad --
